'''Carolina Ödman-Govender''' ({{IPA|de|karoˈliːnaː ˈœtman ˈgo:vəndɐ}}) (3 July 1974<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 Apr 2023 |title=Obituary: Carolina Ödman, 3 July 1974 – 15 November 2022 |url=https://journals.co.za/doi/10.10520/ejc-mnassa_v82_n3_4_a2 |access-date=4 September 2024 |website=Sabinet African Journals}}</ref> – 15 November 2022<ref name=argus />) was a Swiss physicist and academic who was professor of astrophysics at South Africa's [[University of the Western Cape]]. She was awarded the 2018 [[International Astronomical Union]] Special Executive Committee Award for Astronomy Outreach, Development and Education.

== Early life and education ==
Ödman grew up in Switzerland; her parents were Swedish.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/news/science-honors-universe-awareness-spore-award|title=Science Honors "Universe Awareness" with SPORE Award|website=American Association for the Advancement of Science|language=en|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> Inspired by her high school physics teacher, she pursued a career in the sciences. She studied physics at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]] and graduated in 2000.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=22 May 2012|title=Carolina Ödman-Govender (PH'00, DR'03)|url=https://actu.epfl.ch/news/carolina-odman-govender-ph-00-dr-03/ |publisher=EPFL |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.epflalumni.ch/chapters/|title=Chapters|publisher=EPFL Alumni|language=en-US|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.eresearch.ac.za/presentations-2019-day-one|title=Presentations 2019: Day one {{!}} eResearch Africa Conference|website=www.eresearch.ac.za|language=en|access-date=12 July 2019|archive-date=12 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712234208/http://www.eresearch.ac.za/presentations-2019-day-one|url-status=dead}}</ref> She earned her PhD at the [[University of Cambridge]], where she was a member of [[Trinity Hall, Cambridge|Trinity Hall]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.atoptics.org.uk/atoptics/rayim8.htm|title=Crepuscular rays|website=www.atoptics.co.uk|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> She has also consulted for [[UNESCO]], working on the impact of science and technology in society.<ref name=":1" /> She became interested in the philosophical aspects of science; for example, why people are interested in astronomy.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
[[File:Arrival in Hyderabad (1427725363).jpg|left|thumb|Carolina Ödman in 2007 self portrait]]
From 2004 to 2005 she was a Marie Curie Skłodowska postdoctoral scholar at [[Universita degli studi di Roma "La Sapienza"]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://odman.org|title=CV of Carolina Odman}}</ref> She worked in cosmology on several subjects as [[dark energy]], analysis of [[cosmic microwave background]] data, and [[Inflation (cosmology)|inflation]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://inspirehep.net/literature?sort=mostrecent&size=25&page=1&q=find+author+odman,+c.&ui-citation-summary=true|title=INSPIRE|website=inspirehep.net}}</ref> In 2005 Ödman joined [[Leiden University]] as an international project manager, where she worked with [[George K. Miley|George Miley]].<ref name=":0" /> Amongst other achievements, this involved setting up the Astronomy for Africa taskforce and leading Universe Awareness (UNAWE).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cosmoquest.org/x/365daysofastronomy|title=Citizen Science|website=cosmoquest.org|language=en-US|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Ödman|first=Carolina|date=August 2007|title=Making young children aware of the universe|journal=Astronomy & Geophysics|volume=48|issue=4|pages=4.20–4.21|doi=10.1111/j.1468-4004.2007.48420.x|issn=1468-4004|doi-access=free}}</ref> Universe Awareness is an outreach programme that inspires children about astronomy, reaching over 400,000 children in over 60 countries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unawe.org/updates/2018_IAU_Prize_Carolina_Odman-Govender/|title=Special IAU Prize Awarded to First Universe Awareness Project Manager {{!}} UNAWE|website=www.unawe.org|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.unawe.org/|title=UNAWE|website=www.unawe.org|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> She joined the [[Square Kilometre Array]] project at the [[South African Astronomical Observatory]] in 2010. Ödman was made Director of Academic Development at the [[African Institute for Mathematical Sciences]] in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.meltwater.com/za/blog/celebrating-women-in-tech-in-africa-this-international-womens-day/|title=Celebrating Women in Tech in Africa this International Women's Day|last=Dods|first=Philippa|date=8 March 2019|website=South Africa — Meltwater|language=en|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> In 2012 she received the [[Science (journal)|''Science'']] Prize for Online Resources in Education (SPORE) award for her work on Universe Awareness.<ref>{{cite press release|title=Journal Science honors 'Universe Awareness' with award |publisher=American Association for the Advancement of Science |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/908715 |website=EurekAlert! |access-date=17 November 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://woxy.co/video/VT6xxZgy5g8/carolina-odman-govender-ingenieure-scien|title=Carolina Ödman-Govender, Ingénieure Sciences Physiques, 2000 – Video|last=WOXY.CO|website=WOXY.CO|language=en|access-date=12 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712234205/https://woxy.co/video/VT6xxZgy5g8/carolina-odman-govender-ingenieure-scien|archive-date=12 July 2019}}</ref> She was part of the team that created [[GalileoMobile]] project.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://galileoteachers.org/making-the-world-a-better-place/|title=Making the World a Better Place {{!}} Galileo Teacher Training Program|website=galileoteachers.org|access-date=12 July 2019}}</ref>

In 2018 Ödman was made associate director for development and outreach of the Inter-University Institute for Data Intensive Astronomy (IDIA) and an associate professor at the [[University of the Western Cape]].<ref name="uwc" />

In 2021, she was awarded the 2020/2021 [[National Science and Technology Forum]] (NSTF)'s Communication Award,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://nstf.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/21WinnersMediaRelease.pdf|title=National Science and Technology Forum 2020/2021 Award Winners|website=nstf.org.za|language=en-US|access-date=15 November 2022|archive-date=11 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220811084825/https://nstf.org.za/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/21WinnersMediaRelease.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> "for reshaping how science is communicated to the general public and in particular research into building a scientific vocabulary in African languages".<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof Carolina Ödman {{!}} For reshaping how science is communicated to the general public and in particular research into building a scientific vocabulary in African languages. |url=https://nstf.org.za/2022/04/19/prof-carolina-odman/ |publisher=[[National Science and Technology Forum]] (NSTF) |access-date=17 November 2022 |date=2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Haggard |first1=Kerry |title=The NSTF-South32 Awards |url=https://mg.co.za/special-reports/2021-10-01-the-nstf-south32-awards/ |access-date=17 November 2022 |work=The Mail & Guardian |date=1 October 2021 |language=en-ZA |quote=Communication Award:  Professor Carolina Öddman from the Inter-University Institute for Data Intensive Astronomy at the University of the Western Cape (UWC) won for her outstanding promotion of academic research and teaching in science for development. She made significant contributions to the multi-disciplinary research into building a scientific vocabulary in African languages at UWC. ...}}</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
<!--In 2011,{{cn}}-->Ödman was married to [[Kevin Govender]] in South Africa. They had two sons.<ref name="Scientist 2015">{{cite web | title=Carolina Ödman-Govender | website=Ignite – Global Fund for Women | date=15 January 2015 | url=https://ignite.globalfundforwomen.org/be-the-spark/carolina-%C3%B6dman-govender | access-date=17 November 2022}}</ref><ref name="Shaikh 2016">{{cite web | last=Shaikh | first=Nabeelah | title=Gazing at the stars pays off for KZN man | website=IOL | date=27 March 2016 | url=https://www.iol.co.za/news/south-africa/kwazulu-natal/gazing-at-the-stars-pays-off-for-kzn-man-2001891 | access-date=17 November 2022}}</ref>

In early 2018, Ödman was diagnosed with [[pancreatic adenocarcinoma]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://carolune.org/cancer/|title=Carolina Ödman|website=carolune.org|language=en-US|access-date=15 November 2022|archive-date=16 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221116002708/https://carolune.org/cancer/}}</ref><!--She continued to work and travel through her illness and treatment cycles.{{Cn|date=November 2022}}--> She died in [[Cape Town]] on 15 November 2022, at the age of 48.<ref name=argus>{{cite news |last1=Thebus |first1=Shakirah |title=Death of astrophysicist professor Carolina Ödman leaves loved ones feeling profound loss |url=https://www.iol.co.za/capeargus/news/death-of-astrophysicist-professor-carolina-oedman-leaves-loved-ones-feeling-profound-loss-8bbf92b7-116e-424c-a58f-d98db6c2143a |access-date=17 November 2022 |work=[[Cape Argus]] |publisher=[[Independent Online (South Africa)|Independent Online]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Remembering Prof. Carolina Ödman-Govender |url=http://www.africanastronomicalsociety.org/2022/11/16/passing-of-prof-caroline-odman/ |website=African Astronomical Society |date=16 November 2022 |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref><!--<ref>{{cite web |title=With great sadness, we communicate the passing of our colleague and friend, Carolina Ödman-Govender. Carolina was an Associate Professor at the UWC and Associate Director: Development & Outreach for the IDIA. (1/4) |url=https://twitter.com/IAU_Outreach/status/1592759582195351555 |website=IAU OAO on Twitter |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref>-->
